text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- 10 gunmen shock city as they take over Nairobi's busy Kirinyaga road, shooting in the air, sending police officers and civilians scampering for cover in a 20-minute operation.

- International Labour Organisation data show Kenya is among the top 10 African countries leading in the incidence of child labour and is ranked 6th with 41.3 percent of the total number of children aged 10-14 years being economically active.
- An auditor with Kenya Ports Authority tells a Mombasa court senior employees defrauded the firm of thousands of shillings by flouting tender rules and altering unit market prices.

- The chairman of giant dairy Kenya Cooperative Creameries Stanley Metto and his wife narrowly escape death when the car they were travelling in rammed the back of a lorry along the Eldoret-Kapsabet road in the Rift Valley province.

- The government defends a deal in which former cabinet minister Elijah Mwangale is set to sell his giant Quintin Farm to the state for resettling squatters saying it is in order and that the 300 million shillings requested from the treasury was only for the purchase of Mwangale's farm.

- Foreign Affairs Minister Kalonzo Musyoka says regional ministers suspend a ministerial delegation to Burundi to allow time for consultations pending clarification from Burundi military ruler Major Pierre Buyoya as to whether he is ready to enter negotiations with all warring parties.

- Somalia faction leaders announce an end to hostilities that have ravaged the country following a successful breakthrough in two-weeks of exploratory peace talks initiated by Kenya's President Daniel arap Moi.
- Agriculture Minister Simeon Nyachae says Kenya's weekly coffee export auction will remain and tells growers authorities are seeking ways to end delays in payments to farmers.
